# Task P2-18a: FakeSlskd — a scenario-driven stand-in for slskd and AcoustID for the CI gate

**Phase:** 2 · **Depends on:** P2-00 (verified API shapes) · **Suggested tier:** cheap worker · **Estimated size:** M

## Goal
CI cannot reach the Soulseek network, so the Phase 2 gate in `scripts/smoke-test.sh` runs the real image with a **fake slskd** in place of the bundled binary: `SlskdHost` launches it exactly as it launches slskd (`APP__SOULSEEK__BINARY_PATH`), it reads the same `slskd.yml`, answers the slskd 0.26 API subset Wondarr uses from a **scenario file**, "downloads" by generating **real encoded audio** with the image's `ffmpeg`, fingerprints each file with `fpcalc`, and answers AcoustID lookups for those fingerprints on a second port. It also records every search submission so the gate can prove the Soulseek search budget held. A test tool only: it is never part of the image.

## Deliverables
1. `tools/FakeSlskd/FakeSlskd.csproj` — `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web`, `net10.0`, `<IsPackable>false</IsPackable>`, `<InvariantGlobalization>true</InvariantGlobalization>`, `<AssemblyName>slskd</AssemblyName>` (so the published single file is named `slskd`); packages: `YamlDotNet` (already centrally versioned). Add it to `Wondarr.sln` under a `tools` solution folder so `dotnet build -warnaserror` covers it (it must pass the same analyzers).
2. `tools/FakeSlskd/Program.cs` (+ a few files under `tools/FakeSlskd/`):
   - **Startup:** read `SLSKD_CONFIG` (path of `slskd.yml`; fallback `$SLSKD_APP_DIR/slskd.yml`) with YamlDotNet (snake_case): `web.port`, `web.ip_address`, `web.authentication.api_keys.*.key`, `soulseek.username`, `directories.downloads`, `directories.incomplete`, `shares.directories`, `integrations.webhooks.*.call.url` + `headers`. Scenario from `FAKE_SLSKD_SCENARIO` (JSON path; missing → empty scenario). AcoustID stub port from `FAKE_ACOUSTID_PORT` (default 5031, bound to 127.0.0.1). Log to stdout one line per request in slskd's style (`[HH:mm:ss INF] …`), and on start print `[HH:mm:ss INF] Logged in to the Soulseek server as <username>` when a username is configured (the app's log watcher reads it).
   - **Auth:** every `/api/v0/*` request needs `X-API-Key` equal to a configured key → else 401.
   - **State:** `GET /api/v0/application` → the recorded shape (`tests/fixtures/slskd/live/application.json`) with `version.current` `0.26.0`, `server.isLoggedIn` true (false when no username), `user.username`, `shares` `{ready: true, directories, files}` counted from the existing `shares.directories` (audio files, recursive; missing dirs count 0). `GET /api/v0/server` likewise. `GET /api/v0/shares` → `{ "local": [ {id, alias, localPath, remotePath, directories, files} … ] }` per shared directory.
   - **Searches:** `POST /api/v0/searches` (the P2-01 request body) → create `{id, searchText, state: "InProgress", isComplete: false, …}`; record `(id, text, postedAt)` and the in-flight count (in flight = posted and not yet deleted; keep the maximum). After `searchDelayMs` (scenario, default 1500) the search becomes `"Completed, TimedOut"` with the matching responses. `GET /searches/{id}`, `GET /searches/{id}/responses` (**empty until complete**, like the real one), `PUT /searches/{id}` (complete now), `DELETE /searches/{id}` (204, then 404; record `deletedAt`). If more than `maxInFlight` (default 2) searches are in flight → 429 (real slskd behaviour; the app must never trigger it).
   - **Matching:** a scenario file matches a search when every token of the normalised search text (lower-case, diacritics folded with a small Latin table, non-alphanumerics → spaces) occurs among the normalised tokens of its `path`. Responses group files by `username` with the scenario's `hasFreeUploadSlot`, `uploadSpeed`, `queueLength`; each file `{filename: path, size, bitRate?, sampleRate?, bitDepth?, length, isLocked: false}` (`size` from the scenario or estimated from bitrate × length).
   - **Transfers:** `POST /api/v0/transfers/downloads/batches` (P2-10 body) → validates `options.destination` (relative, no `..`), creates one transfer per file (`id`, `batchId`, `username`, `filename`, `size`, `state: "Queued, Remotely"`, `placeInQueue` 1) → 201 `{batch: {id}, failures: []}`; a file not in the scenario → a `failures` entry and 200 if none succeeded. After `transferDelayMs` (default 1000): the file's `transfer` behaviour — `"ok"` (default): `InProgress`, generate the audio into `directories.incomplete`, move it to `<downloads>/<destination>/<bare file name>`, state `"Completed, Succeeded"`, `bytesTransferred = size = actual file size`, `percentComplete` 100, then POST the configured webhook with `{type: "DownloadFileComplete", id, timestamp, localFilename, remoteFilename, transfer}` and its headers (failures ignored); `"reject"` → `"Completed, Rejected"`; `"stall"` → `InProgress` forever with `bytesTransferred` 0. `GET /transfers/downloads` (users → directories → files), `GET /transfers/downloads/{username}/{id}` (404 unknown), `GET …/{id}/position` (`1`), `DELETE …/{id}?remove=` (204; cancels a pending one: `"Completed, Cancelled"`).
   - **Audio generation** (in the container: `ffmpeg`/`fpcalc` on `PATH`): per scenario file `audio: {codec: "mp3" | "flac", bitrateKbps: 320, durationSeconds, seed, frequency}` → `ffmpeg -v error -y -f lavfi -i "anoisesrc=d=<D>:c=pink:r=44100:a=0.25:seed=<seed>" -f lavfi -i "sine=f=<frequency>:d=<D>:r=44100" -filter_complex "[0][1]amix=inputs=2:duration=first" -ac 2 <codec args> <out>` (mp3: `-c:a libmp3lame -b:a <bitrate>k`; flac: `-c:a flac -sample_fmt s16`), then `fpcalc -json <out>` → remember `fingerprint → identity`. Use `ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList`. (Distinct seeds give distinct fingerprints; a pure sine does **not** — see `tests/fixtures/media/README.md`.)
   - **AcoustID stub** on `127.0.0.1:FAKE_ACOUSTID_PORT`: `POST /v2/lookup` (form body, **gzip-compressed** when `Content-Encoding: gzip` — use ASP.NET's request decompression) and `GET /v2/lookup?…`: `client` must be non-empty (else code 4); a known fingerprint → `{"status":"ok","results":[{"id": <deterministic uuid of the fingerprint>, "score": 0.96, "recordings": [{id, title, duration, artists: [{id, name}]}]}]}` from the file's `identity`; unknown → `{"status":"ok","results":[]}`.
   - **Gate log:** `GET /fake/log` (no auth, loopback only) → `{ searches: [{id, text, postedAt, deletedAt}], maxInFlight, transfers: [{id, username, filename, destination, state}] }` (timestamps ISO-8601 UTC with milliseconds).
3. `tests/gate/phase2-scenario.schema.md` — a short description of the scenario JSON: `{ searchDelayMs?, transferDelayMs?, maxInFlight?, files: [ { username, path, size?, bitRate?, sampleRate?, bitDepth?, length, hasFreeUploadSlot?, uploadSpeed?, queueLength?, transfer?: "ok"|"reject"|"stall", audio: {…}, identity: { recordingId, title, artists: [{id, name}], durationSeconds } } ] }`.
4. Tests `tests/Wondarr.Sources.Tests/FakeSlskd/FakeSlskdTests.cs` (add a `ProjectReference` to the tool from the test project; host it in-process with `WebApplicationFactory<FakeSlskd.Program>` or by calling a `FakeSlskdApp.Build(options)` factory you expose — pick the one that works with two ports; the AcoustID stub may be tested as a separate app built by the same factory): search lifecycle (responses empty until complete, delete → 404), matching (diacritics, token subset), 429 above `maxInFlight`, budget log records post/delete, API key required, transfer lifecycle with a **`wav`-free test path**: in tests (no ffmpeg on the dev PC) inject an `IAudioGenerator` fake that writes bytes and returns a fixed fingerprint; the real generator is exercised only when `ffmpeg` is on `PATH` (skip otherwise), webhook posted with the header, AcoustID lookup (form and gzip form) known/unknown/invalid client, `application`/`shares` counts.
5. `tools/FakeSlskd/README.md` — how the smoke test uses it: `dotnet publish tools/FakeSlskd -c Release -r linux-x64 --self-contained -p:PublishSingleFile=true -o <dir>`, mount `<dir>/slskd` into the container, set `APP__SOULSEEK__BINARY_PATH`, `FAKE_SLSKD_SCENARIO`, `APP__ACOUSTID__BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:5031/v2/`.

## Constraints

## Acceptance criteria (each must be demonstrated)
1. `dotnet build -warnaserror` (whole solution, including the tool) → 0 warnings, 0 errors; `dotnet test` → all pass (paste the summary lines).
2. `dotnet publish tools/FakeSlskd -c Release -r linux-x64 --self-contained -p:PublishSingleFile=true -o .fake-out` succeeds (paste the last line; delete `.fake-out` afterwards).
3. The tests in 4 exist and pass.
